Great place that can help you get the most out Vung Tau.
Sep 2023 • Friends
I'm an Australian who visited belly's over a couple of days while in vung tau. This place is a hidden gem, the food was good and the staff are lovely but what's better is these guys help. They aren't just a come drink eat and go place. They help organise scooters (at a great rate), they help organise transport back to ho chi Minh (cheaper than we could find as toursits) and offer advice for the town. This plus their other guests make Belly's a go to place for any person who wants good people. Highly rate Belly's and when I come back i will be comming here.

Super friendly and welcoming
May 2023 • Solo
As a solo female traveler, I walked into Belly’s bar and was greeted straight away by the owner. All the guys there were so welcoming and invited me to sit with them. Belly’s is a one stop shop. I wanted to hire a bike and could do it from here, the girls booked a bus for me to to get back to Ho Chi Minh and exchanged money for me when I couldn’t find anywhere to do it. I told the boys what I was wanting to do and they gave me directions on going to nui dat, long tan, long hai. There were no tours running the day I wanted to go so I went on my own and had no dramas. Nothing was too much trouble. I will definitely come back for a beer. Thank you all for your help and advise.

Has always been my destination for comfort food.
Apr 2023 • Friends
As soon as I hit Vung Tau and have checked into my accommodation I head straight to Bellys Watering Hole to get my Kiwi fix of comfort food by ordering Bellys mums Kiwi recipe of savoury mince and toast with two poached eggs on top. Normally it's served on toast but I like my toast on the side so the toasts stays crunchy. Any way this time after getting my savoury mince out of the way on my 2nd day in I decided to try his Bangers and Mash for 145k vnd (AUD8.90)(NZD9.85)
Well now I am in Heaven.
At long last I have found a pork sausage that tastes just like the ones I grew up with back in New Zealand. I've since found out they are made in VungTau by a Vietnamese lady who was married to a Kiwi who taught her the recipe. Sadly he passed away a few years ago but she is continuing his legendary pork sausage recipe to this day and I am able to buy them and take them back to Saigon with me. So if you're an Aussie or Kiwi and you're visiting VungTau then I can highly recommend you visit Bellys Watering Hole for good comfort food and traditional roast dinners on the weekends. Lamb beef or pork roasts are always popular.
Warm regards, Dirty Pierre.
